description_en: Temple of Bhairava containing a 14th century inscription.The monument is located on a small hill, south of the Dullu palace (now destroyed). Adjacent to it is the temple of Kālikā (DLK0351).The temple is oriented to the north-northeast. It is built in bricks and covered by two-storied tile roofs. It has a single room, accessed through a door in the north-east wall. This door is covered by large copper sheets nailed onto the wood and engraved with texts and various motifs. Inside the sanctum, a small stepped platform is built along the south-western wall. Various objects of devotion and offerings are deposited on it. The first roof is supported by wooden pillars installed all around the sanctum. The floor of the temple and the platform on which it stands has been cemented.The temple is dedicated to Bal Bhairav, the 'infant Bhairav'. The god is thekuldevatāof Dullu's royal family (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009).An inscribed stone stele is installed against the wall, on the right side of the door. It is inscribed in Nāgarī script and dated from ŚS 127(?) (135(?) CE). The stele's typology and epigraphic features are very similar to those of the stele found a the Bāleśvara Mandira (DLK0340), dated of ŚS 1277 (1355 CE).Archaeological objects such as stone lions and architectural elements are placed in different locations in and around the the temple. They broadly date from the medieval period. The actual monument may have been built in the 19th century, or during the 20th century.A building of the Nepal Police was recently built in the western side of the hill. The presence of this office leads to a lot of coming and going and the parking of vehicles between the Kālikā and the Bhairava temples. A ping pong table made of cement was built 2 meters west of the Bhairava Temple.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_description: An stele inscribed in Nāgarī script is installed on the right side of the temple's door.Bishwo Pokharel recently published the following reading of the inscription (Pokharel 2011, p. 107):oṁ maṇi padme huṁetatpuṇyakalājjīyātpūthvīmallanūpaśicaram | jayasiṁghena bāḍākṣaryabhi nirmāpitā śilā || śrī śā 127(9)||
